chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq and Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to increase in his prayer during the month of Ramadan. When he prayed the 'Isha prayer, he would pray after it, so the people would stand behind him. He would enter (his chamber) and leave them, then he would come out again, so they would come and stand behind him. He would leave them and enter (again) repeatedly.
He said, and he said: 'Do not pray after the 'Isha prayer in other than the month of Ramadan.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's practice regarding night prayers after 'Isha during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) voluntary night prayers in Ramadan, illustrating the distinction between his personal devotion and the later institutionalization of Taraweeh. The repeated entry and exit signify that while the congregation followed, the practice was not initially fixed as a communal obligation, a nuance central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the flexibility of *Sunnah* prayers. It concludes by noting this specific manner of praying after 'Isha was particular to Ramadan, emphasizing the unique spiritual elevation of the month.
